newsitem.title: UK: Racal launches strategic overhaul for group.
newsitem.headline: Racal launches strategic overhaul for group.

text.p: Racal Electronics Plc launched a strategic overhaul for the telecommunications to defence electronics group after announcing a sharp drop in annual profits on Tuesday.

The company said it had called in mergers and acquisition advisers to help it "maximise shareholder value" and refocus the group on three principal businesses and it also expected to cut nearly 1,000 jobs from its worldwide workforce in the current year.

Pretax profits fell to 40.4 million pounds for the year to March 31 from 70.4 million pounds last year, after hefty charges for restructuring its Data Products division. But the total dividend payout was maintained at six pence a share for the year.

The company warned the job cuts meant there would be "a significant increase" in the impact of reorganisation costs on operating profits in the current year, although pre-tax profits would be up on the result just reported.

However it said in the results statement that continuing losses in its Radio Communications division, margin pressure in Telecommunications Services and the costs of rationalisation would "adversely impact" the first-half result.

Following a strategic review, the company said it would now work to concentrate the business on three principal activities: "Telecommunications Services and Data Products operating in dynamic markets and Defence Electronics with growth opportunities."

Racal said its Data Products business was now in shape following a fundamental restructuring last year to tackle what it sees as a fast growing market for multimedia communications systems, expanding at 25 percent a year.
"New products to meet these requirements are being introduced and the initial reaction from industry analysts and customers has been positive," the company said in its results statement.
